perf.summary: Deque only needs windowSize slots, not len; oversized stackalloc risks stack overflow
perf.currentCost: Identical to SlidingWindowMax: stackalloc int[len] reserves 4*len bytes though at most windowSize candidate indices are ever live. Large len causes a multi-megabyte stackalloc that can overflow the stack on mobile.
perf.proposedChange: Size the buffer to windowSize and use ring-buffer indexing (head/tail/count modulo windowSize, mask if windowSize is power of two). The eviction comparison on absolute stored indices is unchanged.
perf.rationale: Reduces stack usage from O(len) to O(windowSize) and improves cache locality; same O(len) time.
perf.risk: Same as the Max variant: requires careful modular wrap and capacity of exactly windowSize. No observable behavior change for valid inputs.

perf.summary: Hoist src[i] load and reduce repeated index arithmetic in the inner loop
perf.currentCost: src[i] is reused but i-windowSize and i-windowSize+1 are recomputed each iteration, and the dst index duplicates the eviction expression.
perf.proposedChange: Hoist int cur = src[i]; compute evict = i - windowSize once; maintain a running output index incremented when i >= windowSize-1 instead of recomputing i-windowSize+1.
perf.rationale: Eliminates redundant subtractions and reloads per iteration on the hot loop; identical to the Max-variant micro-opt.
perf.risk: None for valid inputs; running output index must align with i-windowSize+1 at the first emitting iteration.

perf.summary: Remove unused 'using System;' and AggressiveInlining hint that cannot fire
perf.currentCost: using System; is unused, and AggressiveInlining on a stackalloc-containing looped method will not be honored, making the hint misleading.
perf.proposedChange: Remove using System; and the AggressiveInlining attribute from Run.
perf.rationale: Accurate intent and slightly cleaner file with no codegen impact.
